subject: Duplication enquiry: Clinton Papers vol. 64:14-15 (d'Estaing to Gerard/Holker, 30 April 1779)
body:
Dear William L. Clements Library,

One person directs this project and sends this message; the reading and the searches of the editions are done by AI agents (Claude models) working in an open repository, every step logged. We are looking at an enciphered letter that S. Tomokiyo's Cryptiana list identifies as unsolved: Admiral d'Estaing to Gerard, from Martinique, 30 April 1779, intercepted by the British and forwarded home by Sir Henry Clinton, which we understand is held as Clinton Papers, vol. 64:14.

Before placing a duplication request, we would like to confirm that this item may be copied, and get a cost estimate for a reference-quality digital image, for:
- Clinton Papers, vol. 64:14 -- d'Estaing to Gerard, Martinique, 30 April 1779 (the ciphered letter).
- Clinton Papers, vol. 64:15 -- d'Estaing's clear letter to Jean Holker of the same date (two copies), which we would like as a language and register control for the cipher, even though it is not itself the plaintext of 64:14.

We have already checked the printed editions that might carry a decipherment (Doniol vol. IV and Meng's Despatches and Instructions of C. A. Gerard), by full-text search with control phrases found in each; neither prints the passage deciphered, and Doniol gives only a narrative paraphrase of its news. That search log, and everything else we have, is open at https://github.com/NoAutopilot/cipher-lab/tree/main/ciphers/destaing-gerard-1779 .

[SIGN-OFF]
notes: clements.umich.edu is bot-blocked from this environment: curl 403 and a headless-Chromium fetch both failed again today (26 Sept 2026, hit a Cloudflare challenge and the agent-proxy also rejected a connection to challenges.cloudflare.com), matching the 25 Sept 2026 REQUEST.md finding. No email address could be confirmed by direct fetch, so `to` is the library's own 'Ask a Librarian' contact-form URL (per its duplication-and-use page's own instruction to contact the library first) rather than a guessed address. The owner may prefer to use the researcher-account 'New Request' flow directly instead of email, per REQUEST.md.
